correctness.rationale: For n=2m the rainbow count is reduced exactly to twice a(m-a) plus a fixed-cardinality cut in the threshold graph with edges i+j<=m+1. The cut function has an exact two-step recursion. A piecewise quadratic Bellman comparison has residual at most 1/2, giving a uniform O(m) error and reducing the asymptotic extremum to a one-variable quadratic whose unique maximizing densities are 5/11 and 6/11 with value 9/22. Small-instance brute force and exact rational dynamic-programming checks support each reduction.

originality.rationale: Hegde--Kumar--Pratibha (arXiv:2609.18474) prove unrestricted bounds 9/22 and 8/15 and give a parity-and-interval lower construction, but do not prove optimality over arbitrary colorings with monochromatic evens and two-colored odds. Searches covering rainbow Schur triples, parity and odd/even restrictions, monochromatic evens, the 9/22 and 4/11--10/11 constructions, threshold graphs, and max-cut reformulations found no prior statement of the restricted optimum, its cut recursion, or its stability consequence. The source preprint is extremely recent, so originality remains to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The result rules out an entire natural class of improvements on the current 9/22 lower bound, showing that arbitrary rearrangement of the two odd colors cannot help while the evens remain monochromatic in the third color. It also supplies an exact threshold-graph reduction and a near-extremal color-balance constraint, while clearly stopping short of the unrestricted open problem.
